body.statement: The answer to \(\operatorname{oeq:four-mask-early-kill}\) is negative under the frozen assumptions. There are allowed fixed primitive radii and a legal equal-share four-mask family \((P_\eta)\), with \(s(P_\eta)\asymp|\eta|\) and every local factor restriction of rank two, for which \(\mu(P)=0\) for every law in the model. Hence no alternatives in the same shell can have \(\|\mu(P_{\eta,d})-\mu(P_{\eta,0})\|_\infty\geq c_1|d|\) for any \(c_1>0\) and \(d\ne0\), even though the shells are nonempty.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(q_0=4+\delta\), choose allowed constants \(v_\star=v^\star=v>0\) and \(M_{\mathrm{mom}}=(2v)^{q_0/2}\), and take \(p_c=1/4\) with \(p_\star<1/4\). For the four masks, let \(X_\eta\) have rows \((1,x_t)\), where
\[
(x_1,\ldots,x_6)=(1,2,3,4,5,19/5+\eta),
\]
and put \(\Gamma_\eta=X_\eta(X_\eta'X_\eta)^{-1/2}\). For sufficiently small \(|\eta|\), all four local restrictions have rank two. Compactness of a small closed \(\eta\)-neighborhood and continuity therefore permit a fixed
\[
0<g_\star<v\min_{c,\,|\eta|\leq\eta_0}\sigma_2(\Gamma_{\eta,S_c})^2.
\]
Conditional on every cohort, let \(\lambda_i\) be uniform on
\[
\{\sqrt{2v}e_1,-\sqrt{2v}e_1,\sqrt{2v}e_2,-\sqrt{2v}e_2\},
\]
and set \(\varepsilon_i=0\). Then \(m_c=0\), \(H_c=vI_2\), and
\[
\mathbb E\|\lambda_i\|^{q_0}=(2v)^{q_0/2}=M_{\mathrm{mom}}.
\]
Thus all rank, normalization, covariance, orthogonality, homoskedasticity, local-gap, and moment conditions hold. For nonzero sufficiently small \(\eta\), the relation rank is four, so these points are outside the mask relation-rank exceptional set. The proof of \(\operatorname{prop:o3-strict-inclusion}\) gives \(s(P_\eta)\asymp|\eta|>0\).

Choose any nonzero sequence \(\eta_N\to0\) and set \(s_N=s(P_{\eta_N})\). Since a padded projector relation is a contraction, \(s_N\leq1\), and \(P_{\eta_N}\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)\), so every shell is nonempty. But \(\operatorname{lem:tight-moment-radius-forces-zero-means}\) applies to every law in this model class, not only to the displayed family, and gives \(\mu(P)=0\). Therefore the requested positive target separation is impossible for every pair of same-shell laws. This falsifies the conjunction in the open-ended question.
